subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, I attached a simple worksheet we use to map a customer's workload profile to a recommended dedicated reservation plan. Could you please confirm the two items below so our sizing can be precise?

1) Peak concurrent request rate (RPS) for your realtime endpoints (p50/p95 latency targets included).
2) Typical prompt lengths and expected generation length distribution (tokens). If you have a day-of-week or campaign-based spike plan, flag those rows in the sheet.

I attached the baseline workbook (acme_dedicated_workload_baseline.xlsx) with the columns filled in from our discovery call; I made a few assumptions on batch size (auto = 8), kv cache reuse for chat flows, and a conservative 10% headroom. If any of those are off, let us know and we’ll iterate.

Our goal: provide a recommended GPU mix (e.g., 1x A100 80GB + 4x H100-80GB quantized nodes) and a reservation cadence (monthly vs annual commitment) with rough cost delta for burst/overflow.

Next step: If you can confirm the numbers in the sheet by EOD Thursday, Karhtik will produce a draft reservation plan for review.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_dedicated_workload_baseline.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Everett <tom.everett@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation

Rishi —

Thanks for the worksheet, we filled in the primary tabs and attached our internal traffic export (small sample). Quick answers inline:

- Peak concurrent requests: 220 RPS sustained during business hours, with p95 target = 350ms, p50 = 120ms. Evening batch window shows spikes up to 420 RPS for 30–45 minutes during product launches.
- Prompt lengths: median prompt 60 tokens, median generation 180 tokens. 10% of calls include long-form summarization (~800 tokens output).
- Batch behaviour: our client SDK will batch up to 16 requests if latency headroom exists.

We also noted in the sheet that we have a strict data residency requirement in us-west for the user PII flows (so private deployment + dedicated nodes in us-west is preferred).

Attaching a sanitized CSV of traffic by hour for the past 30 days.

Best,
Jane
Senior Platform PM, Acme Robotics
[Attachment: acme_traffic_30d.csv (csv)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-corp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation

Jane —

Appreciate the details and the traffic export, that’s very helpful. Few clarifying questions before I build a concrete recommendation:

- For the 420 RPS spikes at launch, are those mostly short-lived bursts (~<1h) tied to campaign events? If so, do you have an SLO to tolerate slightly higher latency during those windows or do we need hard latency guarantees?
- For the 10% long-form summarization calls (800 tokens), do those use the same model variant as the realtime flows or a different multi-turn job queue?
- Do you expect the SDK batching to be enabled for 75%+ of realtime calls, or is 16 the absolute max but rarely hit?

Notes on our side:
- Two viable GPU mixes for this profile we’ll consider: H100-80GB (better for mixed large-context generation) and A100 80GB (more cost-effective at steady-state with quantization). We’ll show both.
- We will model prefix/KV cache reuse savings for chat flows — with 60–70% cache reuse your effective token compute drops materially.

I’ll draft a table with nodes, estimated sustained throughput (RPS), expected p95 latency, and estimated monthly commit cost. If you confirm the three bullets above I’ll include a burst/overflow strategy (hosted fallback pool vs reserved burst nodes).

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Everett <tom.everett@acme-corp.com>, infraops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation

Karthik —

Answers:
- Launch spikes: campaign-driven, usually 20–60 minutes at peak; we can tolerate slight p95 degradation (up to +150ms) during spikes but prefer to avoid outright failures.
- Long-form summarization: same model class but routed to a separate queue (not latency critical). We can schedule batch-backed workers for those if that lowers cost.
- SDK batching: expect ~55% of calls will batch at 4–8, 10% will reach the 16 limit. So batching helps but don’t assume full 16 for sizing.

Also calling out a compliance constraint: for the PII flows that must stay in us-west, we need a private VPC control plane with customer-owned KMS.

Thanks — we’re ready for the draft reservation plan. Two asks for your plan: (1) show both H100 and A100 mixes (cost vs perf) and (2) recommend a burst strategy that minimizes cross-region data movement for the us-west PII flows.

—Jane
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix worksheet & throughput validation

Jane —

Great, thanks for the clarifications. Karthik and I will produce the reservation_plan_draft.pdf and an A100 vs H100 side-by-side with estimated monthly commit and estimated overflow spend.

Proposed next steps:
- Today: Karthik to circulate draft reservation plan (will include node counts, expected RPS per node, and p50/p95 projections).
- Tomorrow (Fri): 30-minute review with Acme infra & procurement to align on reservation term (12 vs 36 months) and SLAs. I’ll send a calendar invite once the draft is ready.

If helpful, we can also include a small canary window option (2-week, half-capacity failover) for launch events to limit risk.

Attaching the draft to this thread once ready.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reservation_plan_draft.pdf (pdf)]
